newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends sharply up on technical strength.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends sharply up on technical strength.

text.p: NYMEX crude settled sharply higher Tuesday after technical strength and talk that a barge accident in the Mississippi River would disrupt oil shipments triggered feverish short covering.
April crude settled up $1.14 a barrel at $22.06.

"If you look at the latest CFTC report, the market is extremely short on a speculative basis, so it wouldn't take much to get this market going," said John Saucer, Smith Barney analyst in Houston, noting the large amount of short poistions held by small speculators.
The Mississippi River remains closed indefinitely as workers clean up after a string of 25 barges hit a bridge in north Baton Rouge, Lousiana late Monday, the Coast Guard said Tuesday.

The river was already swollen due to flooding in its northern part. An unknown quantity of petro-chemical product has leaked, and local officials ordered a precautionary evacuation of residents and businesses in the vicinity, authorities said.
April gasoline ended up 2.22 cents a gallon at 67.48 cents. April heat ended up 1.88 cents at 56.18 cents a gallon.

Dealers said April crude sharpened its gains after breaching a strong shelf of resistance between $21.40 and $21.45, triggering buy stops. Prompt crude tested those levels four times in the last month, failing each time.
Prompt crude also broke intermediate-term trendline resistance on a spot continuation chart that extended from the high January 9 of $26.74 through the highs January 30 and 31.
April crude ended the day with $1.38 price range for the day after reversing early session losses.

Prompt crude fell eight cents in the morning but bounced off of $20.84, Fibonacci support representing 38 percent retracement from the $21.45 high last week to last week's low of $19.96 (also a nine-month low for spot crude). The session high was $21.25.
"Crude had carved out a bottom, so it was able to shoot up on short covering," said Al Lindseth, manager of oil and gas hedge programs for GSC Energy in Atlanta.
The most recent CFTC Futures Committment of Traders report that reflects positions as of March 11, shows 312,411 short positions, only slighty below the amount of long positions.
Refined products experienced just as much technical buying after breaking resistance, dealers said.

"Gasoline saw some sustained buying after breaking 66.30. It was just a very technical day," said a New York trader, noting resistance of 66.30 which prompt gasoline finally broke after testing it twice in the past week.
Dealers said, unlike crude, there was a lot traders who bought gasoline long in anticipation of the spring gasoline rally which occurs ahead of the summer driving season.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
